page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 186 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The Intel Xeon processor operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate matrix multiplication and vector operations. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates solid performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1913.0 and a multi-core score of 13540.0. Text processing performance is a notable strength, scoring 2480.0 in Geekbench, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances.

The memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached bandwidth of 1671.9 GB/sec for small blocks, dropping to 139.8 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. This memory density and bandwidth support demanding database operations, with Passmark database operations scoring 12079.11 and Redis SET operations reaching 30.03 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the CPU's AMX instructions enable efficient text generation, achieving a top-tier result of 394.04 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter LLM.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute allocation, the c4-highmem-24 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The absence of local NVMe storage means storage-heavy operations must rely on network-attached persistent disks, representing a potential performance tradeoff. This instance is configured for in-memory databases, enterprise application servers, software compilation, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
